markup:
For a **four-hour outdoor shoot with two LED video lights and one monitor**, I'd recommend a portable power station in the **1,000–1,500 Wh range**, assuming you're using moderately powerful LED lights.

The exact size depends on the wattage of your lights and monitor, plus how brightly you'll run them.

## 1. Estimate your power needs

Here's a typical setup:

| Equipment | Power draw | 4-hour energy use |
|---|---:|---:|
| LED video light #1 | 100 W | 400 Wh |
| LED video light #2 | 100 W | 400 Wh |
| Field monitor | 30 W | 120 Wh |
| **Total** | **230 W** | **920 Wh** |

After accounting for inverter losses and a 20% safety margin, you'd want approximately **1,300 Wh of battery capacity**.

## 2. Recommended power station size

| Battery capacity | Estimated runtime at 230 W | Recommendation |
|---|---:|---|
| 500 Wh | 1.8 hours | Too small |
| 1,000 Wh | 3.7 hours | Borderline |
| 1,500 Wh | 5.5 hours | Recommended |
| 2,000 Wh | 7.4 hours | Extra flexibility |

<caption>Runtime estimates assume 85% usable energy through AC outlets. Actual runtime varies with equipment and conditions.</caption>

You also need sufficient **AC output wattage**. For the example above, a station with at least 400–500 W continuous AC output would provide comfortable headroom.

## 3. Calculate your exact requirement

Adjust these values to match your equipment:

{@body const [light1,setLight1]=DIL.useState(100)}
{@body const [light2,setLight2]=DIL.useState(100)}
{@body const [monitor,setMonitor]=DIL.useState(30)}
{@body const [hours,setHours]=DIL.useState(4)}
{@body const watts=light1+light2+monitor}
{@body const capacity=Math.ceil((watts*hours/0.85*1.2)/50)*50}
<box border radius="2xl" padding={3} gap={3}>
  <grid columns={2} gap={3}>
    <grid-item>
      <label>LED light 1 (W)</label>
      <input inputType="number" value={String(light1)} onChange={v=>setLight1(Math.max(0,Number(v)||0))}/>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <label>LED light 2 (W)</label>
      <input inputType="number" value={String(light2)} onChange={v=>setLight2(Math.max(0,Number(v)||0))}/>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <label>Monitor (W)</label>
      <input inputType="number" value={String(monitor)} onChange={v=>setMonitor(Math.max(0,Number(v)||0))}/>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <label>Shoot duration (hours)</label>
      <input inputType="number" value={String(hours)} onChange={v=>setHours(Math.max(0,Number(v)||0))}/>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <divider color="subtle"/>
  <text color="secondary" weight="medium" size="xs">ESTIMATED POWER STATION REQUIREMENTS</text>
  <grid columns={2} gap={2}>
    <grid-item>
      <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{capacity.toLocaleString()} Wh</title>
      <caption>Recommended capacity</caption>
    </grid-item>
    <grid-item>
      <title size="xl" color="default" tabularNums>{Math.ceil(watts*1.25/50)*50} W</title>
      <caption>Minimum suggested AC output</caption>
    </grid-item>
  </grid>
  <caption>Assumes 85% AC efficiency and 20% extra battery reserve. <Cite refs={["turn613782search1","turn613782search10"]}/></caption>
</box>

For outdoor filming, I'd also prioritize a LiFePO4 battery, a pure sine-wave inverter, and sufficient AC outlets for all three devices. Keep the station shaded and protected from moisture, with ventilation unobstructed.

**One question:** What are the brands and models of your two LED lights and monitor? With those, I can narrow down the capacity and recommend a power station that won't be unnecessarily heavy or expensive.
